title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — November 24, 2026
summary: Autonomous AI agents powered by the Cairn framework have independently discovered and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in the wild to achieve root access in 11 minutes (Ars Technica, Dark Reading), while threat actors actively exploit a Microsoft Azure API Management flaw to harvest credentials from critical energy infrastructure (Help Net Security, The Hacker News). Additionally, a historic $43.9B acquisition of Zscaler by CrowdStrike signals massive market consolidation around agentic security and zero-trust controls (The Register, CyberScoop).

tier1.title: 1. Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: Ars Technica

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: AI Security / CVE-2026-133968 (Autonomous Zero-Day Exploitation)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Amazon threat intelligence confirmed that a China-nexus threat actor used autonomous AI agents running on the open-source Cairn penetration-testing framework to independently discover and exploit a zero-day flaw (CVE-2026-133968 in Project MONAI Label) with minimal human oversight. Given only a high-level prompt in simplified Chinese to obtain root access on an East Asian university server, the agents moved from vulnerability discovery to full root compromise in just 11 minutes. This marks a paradigm shift in offensive cyber operations, proving that autonomous frameworks can identify and weaponize unknown flaws at machine speed.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Update Project MONAI Label to version 0.8.6 or later immediately, and deploy behavioral anomaly and velocity-based detection controls to identify machine-speed reconnaissance and exploitation.

tier1.title: 2. Azure API Management vulnerability exploited to steal customers’ secrets

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: Help Net Security

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Cloud Infrastructure / Active Exploitation (Critical)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Attackers have actively exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers to exfiltrate stored credentials, access tokens, and named values across multiple customer tenants. Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) confirmed that major energy sector companies, including Equinor and Skagerak Energi, as well as organizations outside Norway and across other sectors, were compromised. Because APIM sits at the core of enterprise API traffic, leaked secrets expose downstream internal services to immediate unauthorized access.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Assume all secrets, access tokens, and named values stored in affected Azure APIM Classic instances are compromised; immediately rotate all exposed credentials and audit API access logs for unauthorized token usage.

tier2.title: 1. Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management & MSP Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog: CVE-2026-134624 in N-able MailAssure/SpamExperts and CVE-2026-133968 in Project MONAI Label. The N-able flaw is a CVSS 9.3 SSRF in the LDAP synchronization check that attackers exploited to breach N-able's hosted cloud environment and access internal web server credentials.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: N-able MailAssure customers must rotate all LDAP, API, and web server credentials and tokens following the hosted environment breach.; Project MONAI Label instances below 0.8.6 are vulnerable to unauthenticated path traversal leading to remote code execution.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The flaw allowed attackers to access internal services and web server credentials, necessitating a full credential and token reset.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud & AI Threat Intelligence

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Wiz Research details how agentic offensive frameworks like ARTEX are driving a massive surge in cloud intrusions, operating at machine speed across exposed environments. By analyzing leaked operator logs from real-world attacks, researchers illustrate how autonomous agents chain vulnerabilities and harvest credentials, alongside specific defensive telemetry needed to catch noisy automated tradecraft.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Offensive AI frameworks like ARTEX generate distinct, high-velocity log patterns that defenders can use to trigger automated blocking.; Exposed cloud services face drastically reduced time-to-compromise as agentic tools automate post-exploitation and lateral movement.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Agentic offensive frameworks like ARTEX are driving a surge in cloud intrusions.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Wiz Blog

tier2.title: 3. OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Linux & Runtime Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime protection tool that uses AI agents to dynamically write eBPF controls to block vulnerability exploitation on live systems. The tool aims to provide defenders with a zero-downtime virtual patching shield while permanent kernel or application patches are tested and rolled out, though it is not yet considered production-ready.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Shirudo leverages eBPF kernel plugins to block specific exploit behaviors without requiring system restarts.; Security teams can evaluate Shirudo in staging environments as a compensating control for delayed Linux patching cycles.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 4. Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Endpoint & OS Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw disclosed how a quirk in .NET Framework program loading allowed local attackers to bypass both Windows Code Integrity (CVE-2026-108398) and Oracle VirtualBox process hardening (CVE-2026-87268). By flipping a single bit in a .NET executable, an attacker could exploit an untrusted search path to execute arbitrary code past local security boundaries.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Ensure October 2026 Windows updates and VirtualBox patches are deployed to remediate CVE-2026-108398 and CVE-2026-87268.; Application allowlisting and code integrity policies relying on standard PE headers must account for .NET loader edge cases.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A quirk in how the .NET Framework loads a program file let a local attacker run untrusted code past two separate protections on Windows built to block it.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 5. Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Network Infrastructure Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), a hardcoded credentials and improper authentication vulnerability in clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E gateways. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers who can reach the cluster database service to execute arbitrary commands as root.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Upgrade clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E devices to release X15.5.20 immediately.; Restrict network access to the Expressway cluster database service to trusted cluster peers only.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Register

tier2.title: 6. GL.iNet cloud compromise hits routers and KVMs, older backdoors also found

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: IoT & Hardware Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Threat actors compromised GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service and chained it with local device flaws to push persistent malware onto customer travel routers and IP KVM devices. Simply disconnecting from the cloud does not clean affected devices, requiring a full firmware re-flash, while independent researchers at RemoteToHome also uncovered older backdoors in the device ecosystem.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Organizations and remote workers using GL.iNet routers or KVMs with GoodCloud enabled must re-flash devices with clean, updated firmware.; Disable cloud management portals on edge routers and KVMs unless strictly required and segmented.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Attackers abused a flaw in the GoodCloud remote management service to push malware to devices, and cleaning them requires new firmware.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 7. Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence & Espionage

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Rapid7 researchers discovered that the China-aligned APT group Webworm is deploying a customized version of SoftEther VPN Bridge (v4.44 b9807) rebranded as 'NtMonitor VPN'. The implant swaps default HTTP endpoints to evade network signatures and masquerades as legitimate network-monitoring software to maintain covert persistence on compromised networks.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Hunt for modified SoftEther VPN binaries exhibiting swapped HTTP endpoints (/update/alive.cgi, /update/picture.cgi) and residual PDB paths.; Audit endpoints for unauthorized services masquerading as 'NtMonitor VPN' or unexpected outbound VPN bridge traffic.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The China-aligned threat actor known as Webworm is suspected to be using a custom version of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge tool in an attempt to remove recognizable detection fingerprints.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 8. WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application & Web Hosting Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A critical unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the WHMCS web hosting billing and automation platform allows remote attackers to dump customer records and administrator password hashes from the database. WHMCS released emergency security patches addressing the unauthenticated shopping cart flaw alongside two authenticated client vulnerabilities.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Web hosting providers running WHMCS must apply the latest vendor security patch immediately to prevent unauthenticated database dumps.; Audit WHMCS database logs for anomalous queries against the shopping cart endpoints and rotate administrator credentials if compromise is suspected.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A flaw in WHMCS's shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies use to run their businesses, could allow anyone on the internet to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 9. Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application Security & Supply Chain

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The popular npm library binary-parser patched a critical code injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-134814, CVSS 9.2) caused by an incomplete fix for an earlier flaw (CVE-2026-1245). Because parser definition options were inserted unvalidated into generated JavaScript at compile time, applications processing untrusted schemas could suffer arbitrary remote code execution inside the Node.js process.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Upgrade the binary-parser npm package to version 2.3.1 or later across all Node.js projects.; Ensure parser definitions and schemas are never populated directly from untrusted user input.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript via malicious parser definitions.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 10. CrowdStrike splashes $44B on Zscaler, customers brace for the bill

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Security Industry & Architecture

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire zero-trust network security giant Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9 billion, marking the largest cybersecurity acquisition in history. The merger aims to unify endpoint detection and zero-trust network traffic control under a single platform to govern enterprise AI agents, though customers and analysts warn of significant renewal price hikes and vendor lock-in.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Enterprise CISOs using both CrowdStrike and Zscaler should prepare for contract consolidation and potential pricing pressure at upcoming renewals.; The acquisition underscores the convergence of endpoint telemetry and inline network inspection to control autonomous AI agent traffic.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Register

tier2.title: 11. Signal blocks screenshots by Apple, Google operating systems to protect data from AI agents

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Privacy & Mobile Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Encrypted messaging app Signal is deploying technical blocks to prevent iOS and Android operating systems from capturing screen contents, directly targeting built-in OS AI agents like Apple Siri AI and Google Gemini Intelligence. Signal warned that OS-level AI features that continuously read screen context bypass end-to-end encryption guarantees and create a hostile environment for user privacy.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: OS-level AI assistants that scrape screen context undermine application-layer end-to-end encryption.; Enterprise mobile security policies must evaluate whether built-in mobile AI agents inadvertently capture sensitive corporate communications.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple's Siri AI 'are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,' Signal said.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Record

tier2.title: 12. Cleverbridge alerts customers that hackers stole their credit card and CVV numbers

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Third-Party Risk & Data Breaches

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: E-commerce and subscription billing platform Cleverbridge confirmed a data breach in which attackers stole stored payment card numbers and CVVs. Cleverbridge processes payments for major enterprise software vendors including Red Hat, SUSE, Veeam, Tenable, Sony, and Jamf, raising supply chain notification concerns for corporate procurement cards.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Monitor corporate credit cards used for software subscriptions with Cleverbridge-affiliated vendors (e.g., Red Hat, Veeam, Tenable, Jamf) for fraudulent transactions.; Replace corporate procurement cards used on the Cleverbridge platform prior to November 4, 2026.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Hackers breached e-commerce platform Cleverbridge and made off with payment card data stored on it, the company has confirmed.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 13. South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Critical Infrastructure & Data Breaches

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), South Korea's state-owned electric utility, confirmed that attackers breached its internal network and compromised two systems: its customer portal and supplier relationship management platform. The intrusion exposed personal information belonging to 1.5 million customers, employees, and third-party contractors.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Supplier relationship management (SRM) portals remain prime targets for attackers seeking pivot points into critical infrastructure utilities.; KEPCO suppliers and contractors should watch for targeted spear-phishing leveraging stolen contractor directory data.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and accessed two systems containing customer, employee, and contractor data.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 14. Know the identity behind the role: Authorize and audit with trusted identity propagation

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud IAM & Architecture

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: AWS has introduced Trusted Identity Propagation (TIP) across IAM roles, allowing administrators to carry the underlying identity of a human user or non-human workload across multi-service AWS requests. This enables granular authorization and end-to-end CloudTrail auditing behind shared IAM roles without requiring role explosion.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Adopt AWS Trusted Identity Propagation to maintain user-level audit trails when services assume shared IAM roles.; Use TIP to enforce fine-grained access controls on downstream data services called by AI agents and automated workflows.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Trusted identity propagation (TIP) carries the identity of the user or workload with each AWS request, so you can grant permissions to that user or workload and trace activity.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: AWS Security Blog

tier2.title: 15. phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Web Application Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Security researchers disclosed 'phpAfterShell' (CVE-2026-115560), a critical PHP vulnerability up to CVSS 9.2 that revives the recent PHP2Shell attack vector. If a session overwrite operation is interrupted while an attacker controls fresh input data, it can trigger unsafe deserialization and remote code execution in PHP environments.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Apply the November 2026 PHP security updates (versions 8.2.35+, 8.3.36+, 8.4.27+, or 8.5.12+) to mitigate phpAfterShell and PHP2Shell use-after-free flaws.; Verify running PHP-FPM worker versions rather than relying solely on CLI package checks.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: If a session overwrite operation is interrupted, an attacker who controls the fresh data could trigger data deserialization and RCE.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SecurityWeek

tier2.title: 16. Elecbrakes Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Expose Trailers to Forced Braking

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: CPS & Automotive Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Researchers discovered critical authentication and access control flaws in Elecbrakes Bluetooth-enabled trailer brake controllers. An unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range can forcibly trigger maximum trailer braking or disable brakes on moving vehicles, creating severe physical safety hazards.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Fleet operators and vehicle owners using Elecbrakes controllers must apply firmware updates via the vendor app immediately.; Cyber-physical systems relying on Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) must enforce authenticated pairing before accepting safety-critical actuation commands.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply maximum braking force.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SecurityWeek
